history.summary: Ancient dvikuta (two-shrine) temple at Amargol village, on the Hubli-Dharwad route, dedicated to goddess Banashankari (Vana Shankari, 'goddess of the forest', a form of Parvati said to have slain the demon Durgamasura) and to Shiva as a linga. One shrine carries a stepped-diamond Nagara vimana, the other a Dravida vimana; the navaranga pillars are carved with Shiva, Parvati, Vishnu, Narasimha, Ganapati, Brahma and other deities. It is a protected monument of the Archaeological Survey of India, with restoration underway. NOTE: this is NOT the famous Banashankari temple at Badami (Bagalkot district, ~130 km away); the CSV's 'Hubli' is approximate - the temple stands in Amargol village, ~9 km from Hubli Junction. Sources date it to the 12th or 13th century. Coordinates below are village-level and approximate.

name: Banashankari Temple, Amargol
town_description: Amargol is a village on the Hubli-Dharwad highway, about 9 km from Hubli city. It is best known for its 12th-13th century Chalukyan Banashankari temple, a protected ASI monument.

travel.road: On the Hubli-Dharwad highway/BRTS corridor; village road off the highway
